title: Viva Engage: sensitivity labels for communities (Microsoft Purview)
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing statements and control commands are supported. The two Purview navigation paths reach the correct pages but stop before the wizard controls; extend those paths for administrators following the table.

claims.claim: Labels configured with associated policies in the Microsoft Purview portal can be applied to Engage communities.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Admin-opt-in describes the prerequisite enablement and configuration before users can apply container labels.
claims.quote: After you enable and configure sensitivity labels for containers, users can additionally see and apply sensitivity labels to containers that support them. These include Microsoft team sites, Microsoft 365 groups, SharePoint sites, Viva Engage communities, and Loop workspaces.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Labels are unavailable for selection until published in a label policy.
claims.quote: Until you publish your labels, they won't be available to select in apps or for services. To publish the labels, they must be added to a label policy.

claims.claim: Container label settings are visible but cannot be configured before container labels are enabled.
claims.quote: Until sensitivity labels are enabled for containers, the settings are visible but you can't configure them.

claims.claim: Enabling sensitivity labels for containers is a one-time procedure.
claims.quote: If you haven't yet enabled sensitivity labels for containers, do the following set of steps as a one-time procedure:

claims.claim: An admin can select an Engage default label in Microsoft Purview label policy settings.
claims.quote: As an example, select a preferred default label for Engage communities in Microsoft Purview as part of label policy settings.

claims.claim: The Engage default label can be more permissive than the SharePoint site default.
claims.quote:
This new default takes precedence over the default label for sites.
Create a more permissive default for Engage communities, while maintaining a more restrictive default for sites.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A configured default sensitivity label applies automatically when a user creates a community.
claims.quote: Admins can set up sensitivity labels to automatically apply during community creation. When a user creates a new community, the default sensitivity label automatically applies to the community.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The community creator can select a different label from the available list.
claims.quote: The user can select a different label from the list of available labels

claims.claim: Users cannot create new labels in the community-creation label selector.
claims.quote: The user can select a different label from the list of available labels, but they can't create new labels.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment: Autonomy; Governance controls
claims.claim: Community admins can change a community's sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Community admins can change the sensitivity label (and hence its privacy setting) of a community.

claims.claim: Users see the sensitivity label in the live community banner.
claims.quote: After the community is live, the sensitivity label appears to users in the community banner:

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A label's Public or Private setting sets and locks container privacy.
claims.quote: The settings of Public or Private set and lock the privacy setting when you apply this label to the container.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Changing the locked privacy value requires first removing the container label.
claims.quote: locks the privacy value so it can be changed only by first removing the sensitivity label from the container.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; controls[1].governs
claims.claim: Container sensitivity-label privacy and external-user settings govern Viva Engage communities as well as groups and sites.
claims.quote:
Microsoft Teams sites, Microsoft 365 groups, SharePoint sites, Viva Engage communities, and Loop workspaces. To protect these collaborative workspaces, use the following label settings:

- Privacy (public or private)
- External user access

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: External user access controls whether an owner can add guests.
claims.quote: External user access: Control whether the owner can add guests to the container

claims.claim: Communities created with a label disallowing guests are available only to organisational users.
claims.quote: Communities created with a label that doesn’t allow guest access are only available to users in your organization. People outside your organization can’t be added to the community.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Items inside labelled containers do not inherit the container label.
claims.quote: Items in these containers however, do not inherit the labels

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A container label does not apply item-level content markings to its contents.
claims.quote: Items in these containers however, do not inherit the labels and therefore don't apply any item-level label settings, such as content markings and encryption.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A container label does not apply item-level encryption to its contents.
claims.quote: If the label's scope includes files and emails, other label settings such as encryption and content marking aren't applied to the items within the container.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Engage feature page says PowerShell does not directly support specifying community sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: PowerShell cmdlets don't directly support sensitivity labels. Users can't directly specify sensitivity labels for Engage communities.

claims.claim: Applying a label through PowerShell to the connected SharePoint site correspondingly updates the Engage community label.
claims.quote: As a workaround, you can use PowerShell to apply labels to a SharePoint site that connects to an existing Engage community. Doing so causes the label on the Engage community to correspondingly update.

claims.claim: The Viva compliance overview still says Engage sensitivity labels are unsupported, unlike the feature page.
claims.quote: The Viva Engage features eDiscovery and Data Retention are supported by Microsoft Purview; sensitivity labels and data loss prevention aren't supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Engage as public-first in many organisations.
claims.quote: Engage is a public-first platform in many organizations.

claims.claim: Public privacy is the setting Microsoft gives for access by anyone in the organisation.
claims.quote: Privacy: Keep the default of Public if you want anyone in your organization to access the container where this label is applied.

claims.claim: The Engage example uses a General label with Public privacy as its default.
claims.quote: New Engage communities prepopulate with the General label (privacy setting of Public).

claims.claim: Changing External user access applies to new users, not existing guests.
claims.quote: The new setting applies to new users but not to existing users. For example, if this setting was previously selected and as a result, guest users accessed the site, these guest users can still access the site after this setting is cleared in the label configuration.

claims.claim: Publishing external-sharing label options can extend otherwise administrator-restricted site configuration to site owners.
claims.quote: When you configure and publish the label settings for external sharing options and the authentication context, a site owner can now set and change these options for a site by applying or changing the sensitivity label for a team or site.

claims.claim: Publishing authentication-context label options can likewise let site owners change that configuration.
claims.quote: When you configure and publish the label settings for external sharing options and the authentication context, a site owner can now set and change these options for a site by applying or changing the sensitivity label for a team or site.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises allowing 24 hours for label and policy changes before troubleshooting.
claims.quote: For labels and label policy settings, allow 24 hours for the changes to propagate through the services.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The container-label documentation advises against changing applied labels' site and group settings.
claims.quote: As a best practice, don't change the site and group settings for a sensitivity label after the label has been applied to teams, groups, or sites.

claims.claim: The container-label documentation says to wait at least 24 hours if those settings are changed.
claims.quote: If you do, remember to wait at least 24 hours for the changes to replicate to all containers that have the label applied.

claims.claim: The Entra page instead says published group-setting changes are not automatically applied to labelled groups.
claims.quote: When you make changes to group settings for a published label in the Microsoft Purview portal, those policy changes aren't automatically applied on the labeled groups.

claims.claim: The Entra page calls for manually applying updates to affected groups when changes are necessary.
claims.quote: If you must make a change, use a PowerShell script to manually apply updates to the affected groups. This method makes sure that all existing groups enforce the new setting.

claims.claim: The container page warns that deleting a site-and-group label still in policies can cause creation failures.
claims.quote: If you delete a sensitivity label that has the site and group settings enabled, and that label is included in one or more label policies, this action can result in creation failures for new teams, groups, and sites.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft's safe-deletion guidance first removes the label from all policies containing it.
claims.quote: Remove the sensitivity label from all label policies that include the label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The next safe-deletion step waits at least one hour.
claims.quote: Wait at least one hour.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The deletion procedure tests team, group or site creation and confirms the label is no longer visible.
claims.quote: After this wait period, try creating a team, group, or site and confirm that the label is no longer visible.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The label is deleted only after it is no longer visible in that test.
claims.quote: If the sensitivity label isn't visible, you can now safely delete the label.

claims.claim: Users require appropriate sensitivity-labelling licences.
claims.quote: A number of different per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365 apps and services, and the licensing requirements for users depend on the features you use.

claims.claim: Information Protection for Office 365 and AIP require assignment of Standard/Plan 1 alongside Premium/Plan 2.
claims.quote: A standard/Plan 1 license must be assigned in addition to the premium/P2 license for users to have access to sensitivity labeling for Information Protection for Office 365 and AIP, even if the premium licenses/Plan 2 are assigned.

claims.claim: A user assigned AIP P2 must also have AIP P1 assigned.
claims.quote: And if AIP P2 is assigned to a user, that user must also have AIP P1 assigned.

claims.claim: The service description also states sensitivity labelling, including automatic or policy-based labelling, requires Microsoft 365 E5 or IPG.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.claim: Admins need a licence to manage sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Admins also need a license to manage sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator or Security Administrator role groups can provide label-management permissions.
claims.quote: Another option is to add users to the Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator, or Security Administrator role group.

claims.claim: A custom role group containing Sensitivity Label Administrator is another option.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using the default role groups, you can create a new role group and add the Sensitivity Label Administrator role to this group.

claims.claim: Label-creation and policy-configuration permissions are not required merely to apply labels.
claims.quote: These permissions are required only to create and configure sensitivity labels and their label policies. They are not required to apply the labels in apps or services.

claims.claim: Users assigned a publishing policy containing a label can select that label for sites and groups.
claims.quote: The users who are assigned a sensitivity label policy that includes this label will be able to select it for sites and groups.

claims.where: Scope; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Group labels require the Groups & sites label scope.
claims.quote: The sensitivity label scope must be configured for Groups & Sites.

claims.where: Scope; controls[0].governs; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: EnableMIPLabels must be True for Microsoft 365 group label support.
claims.quote: The feature is enabled and EnableMIPLabels is set to True in the Microsoft Graph PowerShell module.

claims.claim: Execute-AzureAdLabelSync in Security & Compliance PowerShell synchronises sensitivity labels to Entra ID.
claims.quote: Labels are synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID with the Execute-AzureAdLabelSync cmdlet in the Security & Compliance PowerShell module.

claims.claim: Labels can take up to 24 hours after synchronisation to become available to Entra ID.
claims.quote: It can take up to 24 hours after synchronization for the label to be available to Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: Microsoft's container pilot first uses a label policy for a few test users.
claims.quote: After you create and configure the sensitivity label, add this label to a label policy that applies to just a few test users.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends publishing-policy groups rather than individual users for lower administrative maintenance.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings. For lower administrative maintenance, groups are recommended rather than individual users.

claims.claim: Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId $grpUnifiedSetting.Id -BodyParameter $params enables group label support when the body sets EnableMIPLabels to True.
A tenant UI for the group/container EnableMIPLabels prerequisite is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: EnableMIPLabels enable sensitivity labels containers admin center UI enable. Read Assign sensitivity labels to Microsoft 365 groups in Microsoft Entra ID and the container-label enablement instructions; they give PowerShell, not an enablement UI.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels reaches the labels page for configuring privacy and guest access.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels
claims.fix: The path stops on the correct page. Extend it for an existing label to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label > Define the scope for this label > Groups & sites > Define protection settings for groups and sites > Privacy and external user access settings > Privacy'. The same wizard also has the External user access control. The first part is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels and the wizard settings at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites; both are already cited.

claims.claim: The printed New-Label call creates a Site, UnifiedGroup label with site-and-group protection enabled, Public or Private privacy, and Boolean guest access.
claims.quote:
The SiteAndGroupProtectionAllowAccessToGuestUsers parameter enables or disables access to guest users. Valid values are:
- $true: Guest access is enabled.
- $false: Guest access is disabled.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies reaches the page for publishing selected labels to users and groups.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies.
On the Label policies page, select Publish label to start the Create policy configuration.
claims.fix: Extend controls[2].ui.path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label > Choose sensitivity labels to publish'. This completes the route to choosing the labels included in the policy, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels.

claims.claim: New-LabelPolicy -Name <policy name> -Labels <label names> creates a policy containing named labels without explicitly selecting recipients or a container default.
claims.quote:
New-LabelPolicy -Name "Research and Development" -Labels "R and D","R and D Management"
This example creates the sensitivity label policy named Research and Development that contains sensitivity labels named R and D and R and D Management.

claims.claim: Policy wizard settings match the scope of the labels selected.
claims.quote: The policy settings that you see match the scope of the labels that you selected.

claims.claim: Within an Engage community, More (...) > Settings leads to the Engage and site label dropdowns, whose choices depend on policies.
claims.quote:
Open the community, select the More menu (...), and choose Settings.
(Depending on how the policies are configured, other choices might be available for each of the two dropdowns.)

claims.quote: Searched: Engage default Set-LabelPolicy; Viva Engage default sensitivity label policy setting name. claims.claim: What publishing an Engage default does to existing unlabelled communities remains undocumented in the pages checked.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage default sensitivity label policy setting name existing unlabeled communities licensing requirements. Read Sensitivity labels in Viva Engage and the label-policy instructions; they describe defaults during creation, not retroactive labelling of unlabelled communities.

claims.claim: Specific event names for applying or changing an Engage community label remain an open question, not a claim that label activities are unaudited.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage sensitivity labels audit events applied changed community audit log activities. Read audit-log-activities (Engage and label sections) and the container page: group labels use Entra auditing, but no Engage-specific event mapping is given.

claims.claim: No additional licence specifically named for labelling Engage communities was found beyond the documented general requirements.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage sensitivity licensing; Viva Engage default sensitivity label policy setting name existing unlabeled communities licensing requirements. Read Engage feature/service pages, Purview service description and group-label prerequisites; no Engage-specific SKU.

claims.claim: The Engage default label takes precedence over the default label for sites.
